_note: POSITIVE flagship playbook for the DRY / ABSTRACT / COMPUTATIONAL topic — the analogue of cinematographer/references/cinematic_recipes.json and interaction_playbook.json, but for chart-led / statistical / non-photographic stories (finance, web analytics, elections, pure statistics, logistics, benchmarks). It exists because the visual branch has rich positive scaffolding (cinematic_recipes.json + the >=5-image target + the BGM ladder) while the abstract branch was only ever phrased negatively ('skip / off / stay light'). A topic with no photographable subject is a FIRST-CLASS flagship target, NOT a lesser fallback: it just wins on a DIFFERENT axis — a sharp reframe, one signature annotated chart, the reader's own position in the data, strong typographic structure, and the runnable-verify layer (which FAVORS computational topics). Read this whenever the topic_profile resolves is_visual=false (especially is_computational=true). ONE self-contained index.html, no build step, runs on file://. Allowed CDNs = Vega-Embed, Leaflet, D3, PDF.js, Pyodide. The Editor + Imagineer read this to pick the engagement + narrative moves; the Designer + Programmer build them.

framing.first_class_target: A dry / abstract topic is a FLAGSHIP target, not a quota to satisfy with the lights off. The bar is the same — a piece a real person wants to read and walks away thinking differently — only the WINNING levers change: NOT real photography (there are no photogenic subjects), but a counter-intuitive reframe, one signature annotated chart, the reader's own position in the numbers, disciplined typography, and the runnable proof. The immersive layer is NOT off, though: cinematic + BGM are mandatory and simply ADAPT — a `data_driven` chart-spine / restrained `generative` cinematic scroll + a restrained real BGM, instead of the photographic immersion a visual topic gets. Aim for excellence; do not aim for 'acceptable given there are no photos'.
framing.the_axis_it_wins_on: Visual stories win on imagery and immersion; abstract stories win on INSIGHT DENSITY + TRANSPARENCY. The strongest dry pieces (FiveThirtyEight forecasts, Economist data essays, Pudding's number-led pieces, an Our-World-in-Data explainer) carry the whole page on a sharp argument, clean structure, and one chart you cannot look away from — with zero decorative photos. That is the target.
framing.honest_restraint: Restraint is preserved on the PHOTO axis, NOT abandoned: do not source decorative stock photos to fill an image quota, do not force a centerpiece onto a finding the reader can't produce. Excellence here is addition of the RIGHT levers (reframe, annotated chart, personal position, verify), not addition of decoration. BUT the immersive layer is no longer optional: cinematic + BGM are MANDATORY stages, so an abstract topic still ships a tasteful immersive layer — a `data_driven` chart-spine scroll background (built from the page's own charts/color/gradient scenes, NOT bolted-on stock photography) or a restrained `generative` atmosphere, PLUS a restrained, tonally-fitting real BGM. The inert charts-only column is no longer acceptable; a page padded with irrelevant stock is the SAME failure dressed up. The distinction: the mandatory immersion must be TASTEFUL and topic-appropriate (a chart-spine / restrained atmosphere that fits a dry subject), never the decorative stock-photo cinematic the photo-axis restraint above forbids.

moves._note: Reusable NARRATIVE + ENGAGEMENT moves for a dry topic — what to lead with, what to make hands-on, how to carry the page without photos. Portable across finance / analytics / elections / statistics / benchmarks.

reframe_hook.job: THE opener for a topic with no photogenic subject: lead with the single COUNTER-INTUITIVE NUMBER or a surprising COMPARISON, not a photo and not background. The hook is a sentence the reader will argue with, stated cold in the first beat — 'X is N times bigger than Y', 'most people assume A, the data says B', 'the gap is larger than the entire C'. The surprise IS the image.
reframe_hook.technique: Find the finding that most VIOLATES intuition (Editor Step 2). State it as a bare, vivid number in the standfirst/first paragraph — but if there is an interactive centerpiece the reader is meant to PRODUCE, prime the question without spoiling the reveal (see interaction_playbook centerpiece_doctrine + editor standfirst rule). Pair the number with a one-line stake ('and that decides who…'), then immediately show the signature chart. Typography does the dramatizing: set the headline number BIG in the display face (see typography.json), not buried in a sentence.
reframe_hook.generalize: finance = 'this rate move erases a year of returns'; analytics = 'one tracker follows you across N of your last M sites'; elections = 'a 2-point swing flips K seats'; statistics = 'the median hides that half the field is below X'. Pick the field's most surprising single comparison and open on it.
reframe_hook.when: ALWAYS the default open for is_visual=false. Never open a dry piece with throat-clearing background — earn the read with the surprising number in beat one.

personal_position.job: The DEFAULT engagement lever for any dry topic with rows a reader fits into: make the aggregate ABOUT THEM. They enter their own value (income, age, region, category, score, year) and the chart highlights WHERE THEY LAND — 'you're here', 'you're in the 73rd percentile', 'your bracket pays X'. Turns a distribution into a personal position and is the single highest-value move for a non-visual page.
personal_position.technique: Realize via interaction_playbook recipe `personal_input_where_you_land` (or `personal_input`): an <input>/<select>/<datalist> (>=44px hit-area) sets state -> handler early-returns under Verify (`if (vOn()) return;`) -> render() pulls the reader's row from the inlined data_table (or computes their percentile via a client_model) -> marks 'you are here' on the signature chart and writes the placement as a BARE parseable number in the readout node. Seed a sensible default so the at-rest state is meaningful; ship a <noscript> fallback that still shows the distribution.
personal_position.generalize: income/tax -> 'what your bracket actually pays'; age/demographics -> 'where your cohort sits'; region/place -> 'your area vs the national line'; benchmark/score -> 'how your number ranks'. If the data has ANY column a reader self-identifies with, this is the lever.
personal_position.when: Whenever the dataset has rows/a continuum a reader can locate themselves in. This is the engagement FLOOR for a purely-descriptive dry topic (see engagement_floor) and a strong supporting playground even when the hero is an explorable.

signature_annotated_chart.job: The centerpiece of a dry page is ONE signature chart that carries the whole argument — and it is ANNOTATED, not a bare plot. Direct-labeled, the key datum highlighted, the surprise called out on the chart itself so a reader who only looks at the picture still gets the point. This is the abstract topic's equivalent of the cinematic hero image.
signature_annotated_chart.technique: Pick the lead finding's data_table. Build ONE chart that is unmistakably the hero (larger, given room, top of the evidence section). Direct-label the important series at its end (no hunting a legend); highlight the one datum the headline is about (a bold mark, a contrasting accent color, a callout box); annotate the surprise IN the chart (an arrow + a short text note: 'this is the gap', 'the line crosses here'). Use the accent color for the one thing that matters and mute everything else (see design_tokens accent discipline). Keep axes honest (zero baseline for bars; label units). Prefer a single, legible chart over a dashboard of small ones.
annotation_devices: Direct labeling: put the series name at the end of its line/bar, drop the legend.
Highlight-one: render every mark in --muted and the ONE key mark in --accent so the eye lands where the argument is.
In-chart callout: a short annotation + leader line on the exact point the headline names ('the median', 'the crossover', 'your bracket').
Reference line / baseline ghost: a labeled reference (the average, last year, the naive baseline) so the reader reads the finding as a DELTA, not a raw value.
Reorder for argument: sort bars by the value the story is about, not alphabetically, so the shape itself makes the point.
signature_annotated_chart.when: Every is_visual=false flagship. If the page has only one strong visual moment, it must be this chart, and it must be annotated.

scale_and_analogy.job: 'How big is big?' — abstract magnitudes (a budget, a probability, a count, a rate) mean nothing until anchored to something the reader's body knows. Translate the number into a relatable scale or analogy so the size is FELT, not just stated.
scale_and_analogy.technique: Anchor the headline magnitude to a familiar reference: a unit-comparison ('enough to…', 'the size of…'), a per-capita / per-day / per-person reduction ('that's $X per household per week'), a time analogy ('1 in N means once every M years'), or a small-multiple of a known quantity. Where it helps, draw it: a unit-chart / waffle / isotype grid (one square = one unit) makes a count tactile; a 'this bar vs that bar' direct comparison makes a ratio obvious. Keep the analogy HONEST (same units, no apples-to-oranges) and dated/sourced like any other number.
scale_and_analogy.generalize: a probability -> a frequency the reader lives ('1 in 12 ~ one person on your bus'); a large sum -> per-person or per-day; a rate -> 'every N seconds'; a ranking gap -> 'as far apart as #1 and #50'. Pick the anchor from the reader's own world.
scale_and_analogy.when: Any time the lead is a magnitude the reader has no native intuition for (most finance/statistics/logistics headlines).

runnable_verify_as_hero_transparency.job: The runnable-verify / Inspector layer is the FLAGSHIP transparency lever, and it FAVORS computational topics — exactly the dry ones. A photo can't be 'run'; a computed headline CAN. 'Check this number yourself, in your browser' is the abstract topic's most distinctive credibility move, the thing a glossy photo essay cannot offer.
runnable_verify_as_hero_transparency.technique: For an is_computational headline, the Analyst emits a client_model + the Inspector ships a Pyodide run_cell that recomputes the published figure EXACTLY from the inlined data_table (deterministic) — see inspector/ + interaction_playbook same_model_as_headline. Make the verify layer PROMINENT, not buried: the headline number is click-to-source, and the reader can 'Run in your browser' to reproduce it. This is the close that earns trust on a page with no imagery to dazzle. The explorable centerpiece (if any) recomputes on that SAME audited model, so the prose figure, the interactive readout, and the runnable cell are three readouts of one model.
runnable_verify_as_hero_transparency.pairs_with: An `explorable_recompute` / `tune_the_assumption` centerpiece (the reader drives the model) sitting on top of the runnable cell (the reader reproduces the published number). On a dry computational topic, prefer this pair as the hero over any visual treatment.
runnable_verify_as_hero_transparency.when: is_computational=true. This is the single most important reason a dry computational topic is a first-class flagship: transparency is its superpower.

typographic_structure_carries_the_page.job: With no photos, strong TYPOGRAPHY + STRUCTURE + a clear analytical THEME carry the page. A disciplined type system and a confident grid make a chart-led page feel premium and intentional, not bare.
typographic_structure_carries_the_page.technique: Commit to ONE analytical theme up front (see theme_directions) and wire its type pairing into :root. Establish a real type scale (a big display face for the headline number + section heads, a readable body, a mono/UI face for figures + captions + the verify panel — see typography.json). Use scale and weight, not color, to build hierarchy. Give the signature chart room (generous whitespace, a strict column grid — see layout.json). Use pull-quotes / big-number callouts to break the text and re-surface key figures. Numbers are tabular-aligned (font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums) so columns read cleanly. The page should look like a designed essay, not a notebook dump.
typographic_structure_carries_the_page.when: Every is_visual=false page. Typography is the primary aesthetic instrument when imagery is off the table.

theme_directions._note: Which themes.json identities suit a dry / abstract / quantitative subject — the analytical, photo-free palettes. Pick ONE and commit (set tokens in :root). The accent carries the one thing that matters; everything else stays muted.
theme_directions.swiss_international: White field, strict grid, neo-grotesque, ONE hot accent. The default for structured / quantitative subjects — rankings, comparisons, indices. The accent highlights the single key datum on the signature chart; the grid does the rest.
theme_directions.editorial_dark: Premium, cinematic-serious analytical. A strong default for a weighty data essay (forecasts, deep statistical pieces) where a dark canvas + a subject-driven accent reads as authoritative. Charts pop against the dark surface.
theme_directions.annual_report: Corporate-report restraint — warm paper, navy ink, serif heads over humanist sans. For finance / org-metric stories that want an institutional, trustworthy register.
theme_directions.terminal_mono: Monospace everything, phosphor accent. For software / benchmark / leaderboard data where a terminal aesthetic is honest to the subject and the mono numerals align by default.
theme_directions.rule: Tune the accent to the subject (heat = warm red/orange, cool/finance = blue/teal). Use the accent for the ONE highlighted series / datum / 'you are here' marker and mute everything else — accent discipline is what makes a chart-led page read as designed rather than busy.

engagement_floor._note: The FLOOR (not a ceiling, not forced decoration) that keeps a dry page from shipping as an inert wall of charts when a real reader-fits-in lever exists. Sits UNDER the centerpiece_doctrine restraint, never overriding it.
engagement_floor.rule: For the purely-descriptive dry sub-case (is_computational=false AND is_visual=false — a topic with no computed headline to re-run and no imagery to source), do not ship an empty / charts-only page. Reach for ONE reader-as-subject lever on a DESCRIPTIVE finding: a `personal_input` / `personal_input_where_you_land` ('where you land' in the catalog/distribution), a `sortable_table` (sort the catalog on the reader's own terms), or a `scored_quiz` (guess a descriptive figure, then see the real one). These produce a finding the reader generates without needing a model.
engagement_floor.still_restraint: This is a FLOOR on the INTERACTION lever, not a mandate to decorate. The existing doctrine holds: do NOT force a centerpiece onto a finding with no reader-producible payoff, and do NOT add a widget that re-teaches what a chart already says. This interaction floor fires ONLY when a genuine reader-fits-in lever exists (the data has rows/a continuum/a catalog a reader self-identifies with or would want to sort). If NO such interaction lever honestly exists, the page may legitimately omit the widget and carry the signature annotated chart instead — that omission is acceptable. NOTE this is SEPARATE from the mandatory immersive layer: even when no interaction lever exists, the page is NOT a bare editorial column — cinematic (a tasteful data_driven chart-spine / restrained generative atmosphere) + a restrained real BGM are mandatory and still ship. The inert column is no longer the acceptable floor; the acceptable minimal is a clean column WITH the mandatory tasteful immersion.
engagement_floor.for_computational: When is_computational=true, the floor is already met and exceeded by the runnable-verify layer + (where warranted) an `explorable_recompute` / `tune_the_assumption` hero — those ARE the engagement. The descriptive floor above is the safety net for the rarer no-model, no-imagery case.
engagement_floor.decision: Ask in order: (1) is_computational? -> the runnable-verify + an explorable on the lead is the hero. (2) else, does any column let a reader find/sort/place themselves? -> a personal_position / sortable_table / scored_quiz is the floor. (3) else -> a clean editorial column + the signature annotated chart, no forced widget.

anti_patterns: Opening a dry piece with throat-clearing background instead of the counter-intuitive number (reframe_hook is the fix).
A bare, unannotated chart as the centerpiece — no direct labels, no highlighted datum, no callout (signature_annotated_chart is the fix).

Sourcing decorative stock PHOTOS to 'make it less dry' — that is forced decoration, not excellence; a photo-free page wins on insight + transparency. (NB: this forbids decorative stock PHOTOGRAPHY, not the mandatory immersive layer itself — an abstract topic still ships a tasteful data_driven chart-spine / restrained generative cinematic + a restrained real BGM; see honest_restraint.)
Shipping an inert wall of charts with no reader-as-subject lever when the data clearly has rows a reader fits into (engagement_floor is the fix).
Hiding the runnable-verify layer at the bottom as a footnote when it is the dry topic's strongest credibility move — surface it as a hero transparency lever.
Stating a large magnitude with no scale/analogy anchor, so the reader has no intuition for whether it is big (scale_and_analogy is the fix).

Treating the abstract branch as 'skip / off / stay light' end-to-end — that under-builds a first-class flagship target; stay light only where a lever genuinely doesn't exist, and build hard where one does.
